subject: New Subprocessor Addition: Request for Review & Impact Assessment
messages:
From: RegulaHealth Privacy <privacy@regulahealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Evan Liu <evan.liu@procure.regulahealth.com>
Date: Sat, 06 Sep 2025 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Notice: Subprocessor Addition - DataBridge Analytics

Hi Marissa,

Heads up — RegulaHealth will be engaging a new subprocessor for product telemetry and aggregated analytics: DataBridge Analytics, Inc. ("DataBridge"). Effective 2025-09-20 they will receive pseudonymized telemetry generated by customer integrations to support usage reporting and product insights.

Key details:
- Subprocessor: DataBridge Analytics, Inc. (ops@databridge.io)
- Purposes: aggregated telemetry, usage metrics, feature adoption analytics
- Data types: pseudonymized telemetry (hashed user identifiers, event names, timestamps), aggregated counts and derived metrics; no raw medical records or PHI will be shared
- Locations: primary processing US (us-west-2), backup processing EU (eu-west-1)
- Security: vendor states TLS in transit + AES-256 at rest; SOC 2 Type II in place (report available on request)

We attached the updated subprocessor list and DataBridge factsheet. Please review and confirm whether Redwood needs to sign any additional paperwork under our existing DPA or whether this is covered by the current subprocessor clause. If you have questions about the scope or the transfer mechanisms (EU/EEA), loop us in.

Attachment(s): subprocessor-list-2025-09.csv, databridge-factsheet.pdf

Thanks,
Priya Raman
Privacy Lead, RegulaHealth
privacy@regulahealth.com

Subject: Re: Fwd: Notice: Subprocessor Addition - DataBridge Analytics

Thanks for the flag, Marissa. Initial read: our standard DPA subprocessor clause likely covers this type of telemetry vendor, but we need to verify a few things before we sign off to RegulaHealth:

1) Confirm categories of data: the external note says "pseudonymized telemetry" — we must confirm there is absolutely no plaintext PHI/PII being transferred. If there is any chance of identifiers being reversible or linkable to a patient, that changes the risk profile.
2) Confirm processors list and whether DataBridge will engage downstream subprocessors; ask for the downstream list and locations.
3) Ask for SOC 2 Type II report and evidence of security certifications.
4) EU transfers: because processing may occur in EU as backup, verify whether DataBridge will rely on SCCs or adequate transfer mechanism; if DataBridge only processes within EU for RegulaHealth EU data, that is preferred.

Action items I recommend we ask RegulaHealth to request from DataBridge (we can send the list):
- SOC 2 Type II report (most recent)
- Dataflow diagram and details on what data fields are shared
- Downstream subprocessors list and locations
- Confirmation on encryption/KMS ownership and where keys are stored

I'll draft a short checklist response (I attached a template) we can send to RegulaHealth to pass to DataBridge. If they return evidence showing minimal risk (hashed-only, no downstream processors with access to raw data, EU residency for EU subjects), legal is comfortable with this being processed under the current DPA.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Fwd: Notice: Subprocessor Addition - DataBridge Analytics

Quick security notes from infra/security perspective:
- Please confirm whether DataBridge stores any raw logs or only aggregated/pseudonymized outputs. If even short-term raw logs are stored, we should require retention limits and a deletion SLA.
- Encryption: ask whether they control their KMS or if keys are managed by a cloud provider; confirm AES-256 at rest + TLS1.2+ in transit.
- Downstream providers: if DataBridge uses a cloud provider in APAC for processing, that introduces extra transfer scope we want visibility on.
- Short-term mitigations we can require:
  * Token scoping so DataBridge tokens only allow read access to telemetry endpoints (no writes to customer data stores)
  * IP allowlisting for ingestion endpoints
  * Minimum retention window (e.g., 30 days) with automatic purge unless otherwise approved

If you want, I can draft a short tech checklist to include with Neha's questionnaire.

Dev Patel
Principal Security Engineer, Serving Runtime

Subject: Re: Notice: Subprocessor Addition - DataBridge Analytics — Follow-up Questions and Request for Evidence

Hi Priya / Evan / DataBridge team,

Thanks for the notice. A few clarifying questions from Redwood's side so we can confirm coverage under our DPA and respond to RegulaHealth's procurement team: 

1) Can DataBridge confirm whether the telemetry is strictly pseudonymized (one-way hashed identifiers) and that there is no access to raw identifying attributes or PII/PHI? If reversible identifiers are used, please describe the re-identification risk and controls.
2) Please provide the SOC 2 Type II report (redacted if necessary) and the most recent security factsheet.
3) Will DataBridge engage additional downstream subprocessors? If yes, please provide the downstream list and locations.
4) For EU subject data, will processing be kept inside EU/EEA, or will transfers to the US occur? If transfers occur, please confirm the legal mechanism (SCCs, adequacy, etc.).
5) Technical mitigations requested by our security team: confirmation of KMS ownership, encryption in transit and at rest, retention limits (suggested default 30 days for raw telemetry), and token scoping options.

We'd also like to set up a 30-minute call with your ops/security lead this week to walk through the factsheet and confirm timelines prior to 2025-09-20. Please reply with requested documents or a proposed time.

Attachments: subprocessor-questionnaire-template.docx (internal checklist)
